summary: Ad-hoc escrow evidence bundle, OIDC session reconstruction sample and SIEM field glossary for legal review
description:
Issue summary:
Northfield Bank (enterprise customer) requests an on-demand evidence bundle suitable for legal escrow that includes: 1) chronologically ordered audit events for a specified user cohort (2026-02-20 to 2026-02-28) with per-record HMAC manifest; 2) a sample OIDC session reconstruction for three anonymized session IDs to support SAR/forensic requests; and 3) a SIEM field glossary mapping (Redwood event fields -> customer SIEM fields) and sample Splunk HEC payload.

Impact:
Customer requires the artifacts for an imminent regulatory inspection. They will treat missing or incorrectly-mapped fields as non-compliant for the audit window. Business impact: potential delay to inspection and legal escalations.

Environment:
Production (us-east) tenant: northfield-bank-prod. Export should include audit events from API gateway, auth service, and the serving-runtime correlation IDs.

Request details / Acceptance criteria:
- Deliver a compressed evidence bundle (tar.gz) containing: ordered JSONL audit events (UTC), an index manifest (per-batch HMAC), and a resume token for each day.
- Provide 3 sample OIDC session reconstructions: input events, derived session timeline, and heuristics used to attribute device/User-Agent and IP geolocation.
- Provide a SIEM field map spreadsheet (CSV) mapping Redwood fields to target Splunk HEC keys and example HEC JSON event payloads (with pseudonymized identifiers).
- Include a short writeup describing redaction rules applied and cryptographic verification steps.

Steps to reproduce (how we will validate):
1) Generate a 48-hour shard for tenant northfield-bank-prod for dates requested; verify chronological ordering and HMAC manifest.
2) Recreate session timelines for three anonymized session IDs provided by the customer.
3) Validate a sample Splunk HEC POST against the customer's ingestion mapping and confirm no PII is exposed beyond allowed pseudonymization.

Logs / artifacts requested from the customer:
- The three session IDs (customer supplied; already received in secure email).
- Confirmation of target SIEM ingestion endpoint and sample index names.

Notes:
Customer explicitly requested the bundle be suitable for third-party legal review and for the files to include deterministically reproducible checksums. They also asked for the glossary in both CSV and human-readable Markdown.

investigation_notes: 1) Export pipeline validated against internal schema v3.2; minor field name mismatch for 'actor.agent' -> mapped to 'agent' in Splunk mapping. 2) OIDC reconstruction requires correlating auth.refresh events with serving-runtime start events using correlation_id and ip_address; wrote a small helper script (tools/session_reconstruct.py) and added to artifacts. 3) HMAC keys rotated on 2026-02-25; we included key metadata in manifest and recorded key id for verifier. 4) Confirmed no model-level content needed for this evidence bundle; scope limited to audit/log events only.
resolution: Work in progress - part1 delivered to SFTP (2026-03-03). Remaining shards (2026-02-25 -> 2026-02-28) in progress; OIDC writeups drafted for three session IDs. Next steps: complete remaining export, sign manifest with x509 if possible, compress full bundle with README and transfer to customer's one-time SFTP credentials. Post-delivery: schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with customer security and legal to explain manifest verification and redaction choices.
resolution_notes: If x509 signing is required after legal review, we will create a follow-up task to have Security Ops sign manifests (linked INT ticket). Customer asked for retention window note; advised that exported files are ephemeral on our SFTP and will be removed after 14 days unless they request extension.
